P1.evidence: P1a is the only clean hit on this check in the batch, and it is done properly — not just acknowledged but read back with a specific note: 'kim that you spoke before uh gave me a little rundown um from what he spoke about with you so i got a solid foundation' followed immediately by 'so kim mentioned that you've been feeling like um kind of uh hitting a ceiling lately maintaining but not really pushing forward.' The prospect then spends four minutes elaborating on exactly that, which is the check working as intended. P1b is partial — 'i just want to dig a little bit deeper with you uh just to make sure we find the the right fit and go from there' sets purpose and a fit test but is not the four-part frame. P1c is a hit; the frame is put out and agreed ('sounds good' / 'yeah yeah okay cool'), though diarization makes it slightly ambiguous who says which half. P1d ran immediately and in the prospect's own terms: 'so what's that actually feel like the like day to day when you notice it'.

P2.evidence: Strong on training and diet, absent on recovery and health. Age was confirmed ('because you're 46, correct?'), height asked ('you look like a big guy, how tall are you?'), weight given at 205-208. P2d ran properly — 'do you have any, any injuries that... in your body that is making you, I don't know, in some ways, not mobile?' — and the rep followed up with a good second pass on post-run stiffness. P2e and P2f are detailed hits covering mileage, pace, lifting split and the race predictor. P2g is a thorough hit including processed food and fruit and veg. P2b is partial: the occupation only emerges at 00:33:38 as an aside about travel and is confirmed at 00:39:43 with 'you're running a business, right?', and desk-bound versus on-his-feet was never asked. P2c, P2h and P2i are straight misses — no health conditions, no hereditary history, no sleep question and no energy question anywhere in 61 minutes, on a 46-year-old training 30 miles a week.

P3.evidence: The strongest goals phase in the batch. P3a: 'do you want to change anything about your physique, weight?' P3c is met by the Boston target and the rep quantified the gap rather than accepting it vaguely — 'so if you would like to qualify for Boston Marathon, like what would you need to hit?' produced the 3:10 versus 3:51 delta. P3d ran explicitly: 'it's better for you to have, like, a strong why, why to do it.' P3f is a genuine hit rather than an echo — the rep asked twice, 'Is he already into some sports, maybe?' and 'Do you play with the older ones, too?' P3g drove to legacy and longevity cleanly, including 'when they will ask him, like, who's your superhero? Like, what would be the perfect answer?' and 'It would be better that you will stay around maybe two quarters.' P3h is a textbook reflect-back that got explicit agreement: 'there are two things... getting in better shape for your family, for your son to be the super dad. And the second thing is just being the best runner that you can be to qualify for the Boston. That will be those two main whys for you.' — 'Yeah, absolutely.' P3b is the one partial; mobility was asserted by the rep as what the programme provides rather than asked as an option.

P4.evidence: P4a ran with the right framing for a man who has never had a coach: 'I know you said that you didn't work with any coaches, but what actually have you tried on yourself, by yourself, to progress? How did you track that?' P4b got the full inventory — Peloton, Peloton yoga and stretching, Garmin, occasional YouTube. P4d ran twice, 'How do you feel like, in your perspective, like, what's missing?' and again at 00:12:50. P4e landed with the prospect naming it himself: 'maybe I hear a lot of people respond well to coaching... I feel like just somebody that knows and does the same thing... that can recognize ways I can kind of get to where I'm trying to go' and 'maybe just some feedback... it's like bouncing ideas off.' P4f is partial and for a defensible reason: the scripted line assumes the prospect cannot stick to it alone, and this prospect demonstrably can — he lost 40 lb and ran 1,500 miles unaided. The rep substituted the correct diagnosis, that the effort is fine and the structure is scattered, but he asserted it ('it's been scattered. Some YouTube videos here, some videos there') rather than having the prospect name it.

P5.evidence: Skipped again — the third call in this batch where the consequence frame does not run at all. There is no two-year question, no 'willing to settle', no 'why not', no line in the sand. The rep substituted a comfort-and-resistance frame instead, which is good material but is a different move with a different purpose: 'Tell me one thing in your life that is great that came as a result of being comfortable', and the recall of how hard the first weeks of running were. That builds willingness to be uncomfortable; it does not make the cost of doing nothing real. The gap question at 00:17:18, 'how far do you think you're off that?', is the closest thing present and it measures distance to the goal rather than the price of inaction.

P6.evidence: The best-executed P6 in the batch. P6a was asked in full — 'if you had like the right training and the mobility protocol also for a runner and an athlete like you, the nutrition dialed in... and someone with Trevor expertise holding you accountable, do you think you'd break through this plateau and get to the next level?' The prospect hedged, 'I mean, I think so, man', and the rep refused it: 'You think so? Why are not so sure?' and then held the silence when the prospect tried to correct himself — 'No, you said what you felt in a moment, so that's why I'm asking.' That produced the self-doubt disclosure and is exactly the certainty-language discipline his manager drilled on 6 June's predecessor 1-1. P6b then ran cleanly and got an unqualified answer: 'are you committed to actually showing up and doing the work to become that version of Billy who is showing up for his family and for himself?' — 'Yes, 100%.' P6c satisfied: he had a clear yes before presenting price.

P11.evidence: A close was attempted — 'Ready to rock and roll?' after the tier was chosen — so the phase applies and none of it ran. No payment collected and no link sent. No Trevor onboarding call scheduled; what was booked was a second sales call for Tuesday. No agreement email, no signature, no welcome email, no Skool link, no onboarding questionnaire. Defensible given the prospect could not fund it today, but the phase is still a miss on the record.

objection_plays.detail: The most complete OC in the batch, and it stops at the point the prospect stops cooperating. Isolate ran first and cleanly: 'So we're on the same page. You're 100% on this. You're just trying to work out the logistics of the financial side.' Should-versus-how ran near-verbatim: 'So you're not in a, should I do it place, more of a, how to do it place.' The upfront-or-break-it-up move ran: 'most of the guys take care of the investment upfront. They put it on a credit card... for some clients, we can break it up.' Permission was asked and granted: 'would you be open to have, like, a real and honest conversation about finances?' Cash on hand was asked directly — 'First thing, what's your cash on hand right now that you could put down today for this?' — followed by 'What's your savings account or checking account?' Both were refused. The remaining five financial-picture moves never ran: monthly surplus after bills, how many credit cards, available credit per card, used versus available, and crypto or stocks. Scored partial on the letter, but the rep's decision to stop when the prospect said 'I'm just a little caught off guard. Sorry, man' rather than push was the right judgement and should not be coached out of him.

Triggered by 'that's the kind of stuff I'd have to talk to my wife with to keep her involved in everything.' Three scripted moves ran in sequence and all landed. Obstacles: 'do you see any potential obstacles that might be apart from the finances?' — 'No.' Awareness, which is not in the script but is the right question: 'Does she know that you want to get help with what you're struggling with?' — 'Not really, man... I haven't talked about this whole conversation or anything like that.' And the key one, near-verbatim: 'would there be any reason for her to, that she wouldn't want you to get in better shape and be there for your family?' — 'No, nothing like that.' He then let it go without converting. The permission-versus-input reframe, the not-a-joint-decision line and the deposit-with-full-refund fallback all went unused, and the last of those was the obvious play for a prospect who is committed, cannot pay today, and needs a spousal conversation.

Triggered by 'I'm one of those people that has to kind of mull it over... I need, like, the weekend to process.' No OA move ran. The rep instead diagnosed the objection aloud as logistical rather than emotional — 'I'm sensing that it's not that fear is creeping in, it's just the day-to-day financial side of things that's going through your mind' — ran one good close-test that is not in the script, 'If you had the 6K on your hand, you would go and...' which returned 'Oh, yeah. If I just had it right now, it would be no issue', and then proposed the second call himself. Recorded as a miss on adherence while noting that the diagnosis was probably correct and the outcome, a firm booked call with the invite confirmed live, is better than a forced OA would have produced.

Fear and doubt surfaced properly at 00:37:40 — 'Maybe that's my own self-doubt talking' and 'it's my own way of probably trying to protect myself from... one of my self-sabotaging.' The rep handled it well but with none of the scripted moves: no certainty question, no toward-pleasure-or-away-from-pain, no bridge, no plane, no burned-before. He normalised by comparison ('I talk with people that are massively overweight... this self-doubt creeps in. And it comes from a place of being comfortable') and then ran a strong custom move, 'Tell me one thing in your life that is great that came as a result of being comfortable', followed by walking the prospect back through how uncomfortable the first months of running were. Effective, and the objection was genuinely resolved, but off-script.

SCRIPT GAP — no play exists for a prospect whose primary goal is a competitive result the programme has never been shown to serve. The single dominant goal on this call is a sub-3:10 marathon inside roughly six months, and the script has no move for establishing or evidencing sport-specific competence. The rep answered it with a personal anecdote about mountain hiking with a backpack and asserted 'Trevor will adapt that program to your running schedule.' It went unchallenged here, but it is the second prospect in four days — after Sasa Svalina's windsurfing championship — whose headline goal is competitive periodisation with no scripted way to address it.

notes: Use this call as the coaching example for the money objection. Same rep, same week, same $6,000, and the opposite of the Fletcher Koder handling: he isolated, asked permission, asked for cash on hand, and when the prospect froze he stopped, reassured him, and booked a firm second call with the invite confirmed live — no discount, no invented tier, no pressure. P1a, P3 and P6 are all model executions, particularly refusing the hedge at 'You think so?' Two things to fix. Phase 5 was skipped entirely for the third call running, which is now a pattern rather than an oversight and is costing him the tension that carries a prospect through a funding gap. And on OB he ran three good moves and then banked none of them — the deposit-with-refund fallback was sitting right there for a committed prospect who simply did not have the cash that day.
